Preserve what sinks into lake depths
Control lake temperature stratification
Teach the value of reflection and depth

hierarchy.role: Guardians of specific water bodies and phenomena

types.appearance: Beautiful beings connected to specific freshwater sources—streams, springs, fountains, wells
types.typical_domain: Springs, streams, fountains, wells, freshwater sources
types.organization: Organized by watershed, with river naiads overseeing tributary naiads

types.appearance: Marine beings with fish tails or watery forms, connected to specific sea areas
types.typical_domain: Bays, coves, straits, coastal waters, specific sea regions
types.organization: Organized by sea region, with elder nereids overseeing larger areas

types.appearance: Beings of water in all its forms—mist, ice, steam, rain—often changeable
types.typical_domain: Rainclouds, mist banks, ice formations, steam vents, elemental water
types.organization: Organized by water phase, with cloud oceanids overseeing rain oceanids, etc.

nymph_choirs.recruitment: Born spontaneously from water bodies that have existed for at least 100 years with consistent characteristics; can also be created by higher water deities for specific purposes
nymph_choirs.mortality: Can fade if their water body is destroyed or fundamentally altered (polluted beyond recognition, drained completely), but often persist as memory-spirits or relocate if some essence is preserved
nymph_choirs.worship: Receive offerings of clean water, respectful use of their domain, pollution cleanup, and seasonal water celebrations

hero_champions.description: Children of gods and mortals who performed great deeds and achieved minor divinity. They serve as examples of heroic potential and as special agents for the gods.

hierarchy.role: Serve as exemplars of specific virtues and as problem-solvers for divine-level challenges

examples.name: Herakleides-Pankration
examples.mortal_achievement: Completed twelve labors set by the gods, each testing a different aspect of strength, wit, and character
examples.current_form: A massive, muscular man covered in the scars of his labors, with lion-skin cloak and club that glows with accomplished power
examples.serves: Zeus-No-Raimei as special problem-solver and monster hunter
examples.unique_power: Can temporarily grant 'labor completion' ability—the power to finish any one difficult task—but only to those with pure intentions

examples.name: Perseis-Gorgon-Slayer
examples.mortal_achievement: Defeated the Gorgon Medusa using wit and reflection rather than direct confrontation
examples.current_form: A sleek, agile hero with shield that still bears Medusa's reflection, and a sword that cuts through deception
examples.serves: Athena-No-Senryaku as master of strategic problem-solving
examples.unique_power: Can show any opponent their own weaknesses reflected back at them

hierarchy.role: Handle specific types of heroic challenges

examples.name: Theseus-Labyrinthos
examples.mortal_achievement: Navigated the Minotaur's labyrinth without thread or guide, creating mental maps
examples.current_form: A sharp-eyed hero with mind that creates perfect maps, holding a sword that points toward exits
examples.serves: Hermes-No-Kotsu as guide through complex situations
examples.unique_power: Can always find the optimal path through any complexity, but only for escape or rescue, not attack

hero_champions.ascension_process: Must be born of divine and mortal parentage, complete at least one great labor witnessed by gods, die heroically (or achieve apotheosis without death in rare cases), and have their story told by at least 1,000 bards for 100 years
hero_champions.limitations: Cannot directly intervene in mortal affairs without divine permission or clear moral imperative; often bound to specific geas or limitations from their mortal lives
hero_champions.shrines: Located at sites of their great deeds, burial sites, or places named after them; often become pilgrimage sites for those seeking similar virtues

satyr_sileni_troops.description: Rustic nature spirits of wild places, revelry, music, and untamed freedom. They serve as reminders that civilization exists alongside and sometimes in tension with wild nature.

types.appearance: Men with goat legs, horns, and tails, with wild hair and playful expressions, always carrying pipes or instruments
types.intelligence: Primal consciousness (understand instinct, pleasure, wild freedom, natural rhythms)
duties: Maintain wild places free from excessive civilization
Inspire artistic and musical creativity through revelry
Remind mortals of their animal nature
Protect natural fertility and wild growth
types.communication: Through music, dance, playful challenges, and dreams of freedom

types.appearance: Older, wiser satyrs with larger horns, vine-wreathed bodies, and eyes that have seen centuries of revelry and wisdom
types.intelligence: Elder wild consciousness (understand the balance between wild and civilized, the wisdom in pleasure, the cycles of nature)
duties: Teach younger satyrs and mortals responsible revelry
Maintain ancient wild places and rituals
Mediate between wild nature and civilization
Preserve ancient musical and poetic forms
types.communication: Through riddles, wise sayings disguised as jokes, and deep musical patterns

types.appearance: Women (and some men) in states of divine ecstasy, wearing animal skins, carrying thyrsus staffs, moving with unnatural grace and energy
types.intelligence: Ecstatic consciousness (understand surrender to divine, breaking of boundaries, transformative experience)
duties: Facilitate divine ecstasy and revelation through ritual
Break down artificial social boundaries
Protect sacred madness and divine inspiration
Maintain the balance between order and ecstatic chaos
types.communication: Through ecstatic cries, prophetic utterances, and shared trance states

satyr_sileni_troops.creation: Born from wild places that have never known civilization, or from particularly potent acts of revelry and creativity; can also be created by Dionysus or Pan for specific purposes
satyr_sileni_troops.lifespan: Long-lived but not immortal; can be killed by extreme civilization (paving over wild places) or loss of all revelry in an area; rejuvenate through participation in wild rituals
satyr_sileni_troops.worship: Receive offerings of wine, music, dance, sexual celebration, and protection of wild places; festivals in their honor involve temporary suspension of social norms

daemon_personifications.description: Minor deities who are specific concepts, emotions, or abstract forces given divine form. They make the intangible tangible and govern their respective domains.

notable_embodiments.name: Nike-Alate
notable_embodiments.appearance: A winged woman with laurel crown, flowing robes, and a palm branch, always in motion as if celebrating
notable_embodiments.manifestation_conditions: Appears when a victory is earned through skill, virtue, or destiny rather than cheating or luck
notable_embodiments.power: Can grant the certainty of victory to those fighting for right causes, but only at the moment of greatest need
notable_embodiments.limitation: Cannot grant victory to the undeserving; fades if victory is misused

notable_embodiments.name: Eros-Philtatos
notable_embodiments.appearance: A beautiful youth with wings, carrying bow and arrows that glow with different colors for different types of love
notable_embodiments.manifestation_conditions: Appears when two souls are perfectly matched but circumstances keep them apart
notable_embodiments.power: Can create irresistible attraction between rightly matched beings
notable_embodiments.limitation: Cannot create love where no potential exists; arrows can be resisted by strong will

notable_embodiments.name: Thanatos-Eirene
notable_embodiments.appearance: A serene, androgynous figure with gentle wings, carrying an inverted torch and a poppy
notable_embodiments.manifestation_conditions: Appears when someone is ready to die peacefully and needs gentle guidance
notable_embodiments.power: Can ease the pain of dying and ensure peaceful transition
notable_embodiments.limitation: Cannot intervene in violent or untimely deaths; only comes when death is natural and accepted

daemon_personifications.birth_process: Form when a concept is deeply believed in and experienced by at least 10,000 beings consistently for 100 years; stronger concepts form more powerful daemones
daemon_personifications.power_source: Draw strength from continued belief in and experience of their concept; grow stronger as their concept becomes more prevalent in the world
daemon_personifications.vulnerability: Weaken if their concept becomes rare or misunderstood; can fade into nothingness if completely forgotten

olympian_bureaucracy.description: Divine functionaries who manage the day-to-day operations of the divine realm—scheduling miracles, processing prayers, maintaining divine laws, and coordinating between deities.

departments.head: Euchê-Logistês, Master of Petitions
duties: Receive, sort, and prioritize mortal prayers
Route prayers to appropriate deities
Log prayer outcomes for karmic accounting
Manage prayer backlog during crises
departments.office_location: The Hall of Echoing Petitions on Mount Aetios' lower slopes

departments.head: Thauma-Planner, Coordinator of Wonders
duties: Schedule divine interventions to avoid conflicts
Coordinate large-scale miracles requiring multiple deities
Maintain the Calendar of Possible Wonders
Prevent miracle overload in specific areas
departments.office_location: The Observatory of Timely Interventions, floating above Mount Aetios

supreme_god.name: Dagda-No-Kyoten, The Good God's Cauldron
supreme_god.title: The All-Father of Abundance
supreme_god.description: Dagda towers like a walking hill crowned in runic gold, a colossal, broad-chested Celtic god whose human features are carved with mirth and ancient wisdom, skin sun-warmed bronze etched faintly with glowing knotwork veins that pulse with life; his great belly is not softness but the sacred curvature of inexhaustible abundance, wrapped in layered noble furs and green-gold mail that hums like a granary before harvest, as he strides forward mid-feast and mid-war alike, one armored foot planted upon cracked stone that blooms into grain beneath his weight, the other splashing into mead-flowing rivers spilling from the shattered sky, his titanic club slung across his back forged of living oak and star-iron, one end haloed in grave-silence, the other blazing with rebirth-runes, while the Undry Cauldron floats beside him like a minor sun of steam and healing light and Uaithne circles overhead as a spectral harp tugging the seasons like banners in a storm; his aura rolls outward in golden waves of hearth-heat and generosity so immense it bends reality into feasting halls and fertile fields wherever he stands, proving him not merely a giver of plenty, but the living center of civilization itself.
supreme_god.god_of: The giant, club-wielding god whose cauldron never empties and harp controls seasons. Fatherly protector of Skydrift, concerned with the well-being of all, not just worship. His club kills with one end, revives with the other.
supreme_god.appearance: A giant of a man with a great belly (sign of abundance), wearing a simple tunic. Carries an immense club, a bottomless cauldron, and a harp that plays itself.

unique_abilities.name: Coire Ansic (The Undry Cauldron)
unique_abilities.effect: Can feed any number of people and never empties; its broth also heals all wounds

unique_abilities.name: Uaithne (The Four-Angled Music)
unique_abilities.effect: His harp can make people weep, laugh, or sleep, and can control the seasons themselves

supreme_god.realm: Brugh na Bóinne (The Mound of Abundance in the floating islands)

high_gods.name: Morrigan-No-Yogen, The Phantom Queen
high_gods.title: Goddess of Fate and War
high_gods.description: Morrigan advances from a battlefield that is also a throne room of fate, her human form devastatingly beautiful and terrible, pale skin luminous as moonlit steel, thick thighs and narrow waist wrapped in minimal noble leathers and raven-feathered silks that cling like prophecy itself, her face sharp and regal with eyes that flicker between crow-black void and blood-red foresight, as her three aspects bleed through her body simultaneously, spectral wings tearing from her shadow, a crown of broken spears and bones hovering above her head, and ghostly hands of the crone brushing fate-threads from her shoulders; she wields no single weapon, for the air itself screams with Badb’s Cry around her, banners rot, kings falter, and destinies split at her feet, while the background fractures into overlapping visions of victory and ruin, rivers running backward with blood and sovereignty cups overflowing with starlight; her aura is a freezing, intoxicating mist of copper and rain that grips the spine and ignites berserker courage or absolute terror, declaring her not a herald of fate, but the merciless examiner who dares mortals to defy it.
high_gods.god_of: Triple goddess who appears as crow, washer at ford, or beautiful woman. Decides who dies in battle and prophesies kings' fates.
high_gods.unique_ability: Badb's Cry - her crow's call can terrify armies or inspire them to greatness

high_gods.name: Brigid-No-Shono, The Triple Flame
high_gods.title: Goddess of Threefold Arts
high_gods.description: Brigid stands poised at the intersection of forge, shrine, and battlefield, her human form radiant and irresistibly graceful, warm ivory skin kissed by firelight, her figure strong yet alluring beneath flowing white-gold robes split for movement and adorned with minimal knotwork jewelry that glows like embers, her face serene but incandescent with purpose, eyes burning with triple fire as three spectral selves orbit her, healer, poet, smith, all bound to one body; in one hand she raises a hammer of sun-forged bronze dripping sparks that become runes midair, in another a bowl of luminous flame that seals wounds and purifies corruption, while whispered verses coil from her lips as living script that shapes reality, the background unfolding into a mythic panorama of rising cities, healed warriors, and blades being born screaming from anvils, her aura a crystalline heat that sharpens thought, steadies hands, and sanctifies labor itself, marking her not as inspiration alone, but as the divine proof that creation is the highest form of devotion.
high_gods.god_of: Triple goddess of healing (physician), poetry (inspiration), and smithing (craft). Her sacred flame never goes out.
high_gods.unique_ability: Imbas Forosnai (Illumination of Inspiration) - grants true creative or healing insight

high_gods.name: Lugh-No-Sainou, The Many-Skilled
high_gods.title: Master of All Arts
high_gods.description: Lugh explodes into motion like a festival given flesh, a tall, flawlessly proportioned Celtic god with golden skin etched in faint ogham-light, muscles honed like a champion yet wrapped in noble, layered armor of silver, leather, and sun-threaded cloth, his handsome human face calm even as reality strains to keep pace with him, multiple arms phasing into existence as echoes of mastery, one casting the spear Gáe Assail blazing with solar force, another plucking a harp that mends morale and flesh alike, another inscribing runes that fracture probability; the ground beneath him becomes Tailtiu reborn, arenas, markets, and warfields overlapping in a kaleidoscope of achievement, while his aura crackles with intoxicating brilliance that accelerates learning, sharpens reflexes, and awakens dormant genius in all who witness him, proclaiming Lugh not as a god who knows all arts, but as the impossible ideal where every path of excellence meets.
high_gods.god_of: God skilled in every art - warrior, poet, harper, craftsman. His spear never misses, his sling-stone always hits.
high_gods.unique_ability: Samilgadanach (Equally Skilled in All Arts) - can master any skill upon seeing it performed

high_gods.name: Manannan-No-Uneri, The Sea's Veil
high_gods.title: Lord of the Otherworld
high_gods.description: Manannan emerges half-seen from a rolling wall of silver mist, a broad-shouldered, armored Celtic god with sea-bronzed human skin and storm-dark eyes, his noble attire layered in wave-patterned mail and a living cloak of fog that constantly shifts form, revealing and concealing him like the sea itself, as he rides a chariot skimming impossible waters where sky and ocean fold together, Scuabtuinne cutting through realms without resistance; his helm bears pearl-inlaid runes, his spear drips illusion like saltwater, and behind him Tír na nÓg flickers into view, orchards floating upside-down in the clouds, the background dissolving into a dreamlike collision of horizons, while his aura is a cool, protective vastness that bends perception, hides truth from the unworthy, and carries songs that blur memory and distance, establishing him as not merely a sea god, but the living threshold between worlds, where passage itself becomes sacred.
high_gods.god_of: God who rides chariot over waves, owner of cloak of invisibility and boat that sails itself. Guardian of earthly paradise.
high_gods.unique_ability: Féth Fíada (Mist of Concealment) - can hide anything or anyone in magical mists

high_gods.name: Cernunnos-No-Shizen, The Horned Lord
high_gods.title: Lord of Wild Things
high_gods.description: Cernunnos sits yet dominates all motion, a massively built, horn-crowned Celtic god with deeply human features and forest-dark skin traced in mossy runes, his antlers vast and branching like constellations of wood, his muscular frame draped in minimal noble leathers, fur, and gold torcs that gleam with ancient authority, thick thighs grounded in earth as roots coil subtly from his feet into the world; in his grasp the ram-horned serpent coils and uncoils as a living sigil of life and death, while the forest behind him rises into a mythic cathedral of beasts, spirits, and flowing green light, the sky splitting with auroral leaves and starlight filtered through branches; his aura is overwhelming, fertile, and primal, a slow, thunderous pulse that awakens instincts, commands animals, and reminds gods and mortals alike that all crowns ultimately bow to the wild order he embodies.
high_gods.god_of: Antlered god who sits cross-legged, master of animals. Holds torc (nobility) and ram-headed serpent (fertility).
high_gods.unique_ability: Wild Parliament - can communicate with and command all animals

low_gods.name: Aengus-No-Koi, The Youthful Love
low_gods.description: Aengus appears mid-leap upon a bridge of dawnlight, a radiant Celtic god with a flawlessly youthful human face and sun-kissed skin, his athletic, armor-clad form wrapped in noble white-gold silks and light mail etched with heart-knot runes, every movement scattering luminous birds born from his breath and kisses that spiral into the sky whispering promises and regrets alike; his eyes shimmer with longing and wonder, his hair flows like morning mist caught in sunlight, and behind him the background fractures into overlapping dreamscapes of lovers meeting and parting across impossible distances, while his aura is a shimmering tide of euphoria and aching beauty that intoxicates the heart and softens even divine resolve, declaring him not merely the god of love, but the living embodiment of love’s sweetness and sorrow intertwined.
low_gods.god_of: God of young love and poetic inspiration. His kisses become birds that whisper love thoughts.

low_gods.name: Nuada-No-Ken, The Silver-Handed
low_gods.description: Nuada stands advancing from a battlefield turned throne-ground, a towering, broad-shouldered Celtic king with weathered human features and bronze-toned skin, clad in heavy ceremonial armor chased with lunar silver, his flawless silver hand glowing with sovereign runes as it grips a great sword held point-down in judgment; his posture is unyielding yet restrained, his eyes calm with earned authority, and behind him shattered banners rise and reassemble as if reality itself acknowledges his right to rule, while his aura radiates a cold, noble gravity that steadies armies and silences dissent, proclaiming him a king not born perfect, but reforged through sacrifice into legitimacy.
low_gods.god_of: King of gods who lost arm in battle, got silver replacement. Represents just rule and sacrifice for people.

low_gods.name: Goibniu-No-Kaji, The Immortal Smith
low_gods.description: Goibniu looms within a forge that opens into a mythic hall of endless revelry, a massively built Celtic god with soot-darkened skin and a powerful human face split by a craftsman’s grin, his noble armor layered with forge-aprons and glowing rivets, muscles corded like wrought iron as he strikes a star-metal anvil mid-swing; sparks freeze into weapons midair while golden ale flows through the floor like veins, warriors laughing in eternal health behind him, and his aura is a roaring warmth of creation and fellowship that binds gods together as kin, revealing him as the immortal architect not only of weapons, but of unbreakable unity.
low_gods.god_of: Smith god whose weapons always hit, whose beer grants immortality. Hosts otherworld feast.

low_gods.name: Dian Cecht-No-Chiyu, The Healing Waters
low_gods.description: Dian Cecht stands at the edge of a moonlit well that reflects both life and death, a tall, imposing Celtic god with sharp human features and pale, marble-toned skin, wrapped in austere healer’s robes reinforced with ritual armor plates etched in medical sigils, his hands glowing with icy-blue restorative power even as shadows of broken bodies and resurrected warriors drift behind him; his expression is severe, burdened by knowledge, and his aura is a chilling purity that closes wounds and stills pain yet carries the weight of irreversible judgment, marking him as the god who can restore life, but never innocence.
low_gods.god_of: Healer god whose well restores dead to life if placed in it. Killed own son out of jealousy of better healer.

low_gods.name: Ogma-No-Moji, The Eloquent Strong
low_gods.description: Ogma surges forward like a living siege engine, a colossal, armor-laden Celtic god with a powerful human face carved in confidence, dark skin gleaming beneath bronze plates inscribed with glowing Ogham, his mouth open mid-command as spoken words manifest as physical force, cracking stone and lifting armies; his immense club rests across his back like punctuation to violence, the background bending into vibrating glyphs and shattered battlements, while his aura is a thunderous pressure of persuasion and strength that proves language itself can be a weapon sharper than steel.
low_gods.god_of: God of eloquence and language who invented Ogham script. Also champion warrior.

low_gods.name: Epona-No-Ba, The Horse Mother
low_gods.description: Epona rides straight out of myth into motion, a breathtaking Celtic goddess with radiant human beauty, warm ivory skin, thick thighs and a slender waist framed by minimal noble riding silks and gold tack-jewelry, her hair streaming as one with her magnificent steed whose hooves strike sparks of starlight; her posture is effortless dominance, her gaze protective yet alluring, and the background becomes an endless rolling plain stitched with spirit-roads, while her aura is a powerful, reassuring rhythm of trust, speed, and companionship that binds rider and mount into a single sacred force.
low_gods.god_of: Only Celtic goddess adopted by Romans. Protector of horses, riders, and stables.

low_gods.name: Sucellus-No-Tsuchi, The Good Striker
low_gods.description: Sucellus advances with seismic certainty, a massive, armor-clad Celtic god with deep earthen skin and a bearded human face etched in patience, his long-handled hammer descending mid-swing as the ground fractures into fertile fields and forests behind him; his armor is layered bark-metal and oak motifs, his stance immovable, and his aura is a heavy, comforting pulse of soil, ale, and seasonal certainty that reassures mortals that life will always return, no matter how hard the winter.
low_gods.god_of: God with large hammer (strikes earth for fertility) and pot (of eternal drink). Protector of farmers.

low_gods.name: Taranis-No-Raimei, The Thunder Wheel
low_gods.description: Taranis descends within a spiraling storm, a towering Celtic god clad in radiant sky-forged armor, his muscular human frame crackling with lightning as he spins the blazing solar wheel like a cosmic weapon; his face is stern and luminous, eyes glowing with thunder’s judgment, and the background fractures into storm-cloud temples and burning effigies of purification, while his aura is a deafening, electrified presence that annihilates corruption and shields the faithful, declaring him the terrifying mercy of the heavens made manifest.
low_gods.god_of: God represented by wheel (sun/sky) and thunder. Human sacrifices burned in wicker man for him.

low_gods.name: Belanus-No-Hi, The Shining One
low_gods.description: Belanus strides from a veil of steam and sunlight, a noble, broad-chested Celtic god with glowing golden skin and serene human features, clad in radiant armor polished like dawn, a solar spear-staff in hand that emits healing light with every step; sacred springs erupt behind him into floating halos of mist and flame, and his aura is a piercing warmth that burns away disease and despair alike, revealing him as the benevolent yet uncompromising triumph of light over decay.
low_gods.god_of: Solar god associated with healing springs and fire. His festivals involve bonfires.

low_gods.name: Macha-No-Kyoso, The Horse Race
low_gods.god_of: Goddess who outran king's horses while pregnant. Protector of land and its fertility.

demi_gods.name: Draoi-Fionn
demi_gods.title: The Oak-Speaker
demi_gods.full_title: Druid Who Learned The Language Of Every Tree In The Floating Groves
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Druid from the highest floating grove in Skydrift
demi_gods.ascension_story: Fionn spent seven years in silence, listening to the trees until he understood each species' unique language. When a blight threatened to destroy the floating groves, he negotiated with the trees to share their ancient immunities, creating a cure that saved the entire ecosystem. Cernunnos-No-Shizen, impressed by this respectful communication, infused him with the essence of the First Oak, granting him demi-divinity as the voice of the groves.
demi_gods.appearance: A man with bark-like skin, leaves growing from his hair, and eyes that show shifting forest patterns. His voice carries the sound of wind through leaves. Wears simple druidic robes woven from living vines.

unique_abilities.name: Comhrá Crann
unique_abilities.effect: Can communicate with any plant life, understanding their memories, needs, and wisdom
unique_abilities.limitations: Plants must be willing to communicate; cannot force them to speak

unique_abilities.name: Grove-Mind
unique_abilities.effect: Can temporarily connect multiple plants into a shared consciousness for problem-solving or defense
unique_abilities.limitations: Requires physical connection between plants; broken if the connection is severed

demi_gods.current_role: Chief interpreter for the Floating Groves and teacher of tree languages
duties: Mediates between plant life and other beings
Teaches druids respectful communication with flora
Maintains the Library of Tree Songs
Advises on ecological balance in floating islands
sacred_items: The Whispering Staff (amplifies plant voices)
Acorn of Tongues (when planted, allows temporary understanding of plant language)
temples: The Speaking Grove (a circle of ancient trees that answer questions)

rivals: Those who clear-cut without consultation
Entities that spread plant diseases intentionally
students: A circle of 13 druids learning tree languages

weaknesses: Cannot communicate with completely artificial plants
Weakened in areas devoid of plant life
Compelled to translate for any plant that requests communication

demi_gods.name: Sidhe-Caoimhe
demi_gods.title: The Mound's Grace
demi_gods.full_title: Fairy Queen Who Protected Mortals From Her Own Kind
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Sidhe (fairy) noble who fell in love with a mortal
demi_gods.ascension_story: Caoimhe defended her mortal lover's village from fairy tricks and kidnappings, teaching her people to respect mortals rather than toy with them. When her own court threatened to erase the village from memory, she sacrificed her fairy immortality to create a permanent protection ward. Brigid-No-Shono, goddess of threefold arts, was moved by this selfless love and restored her as a demi-goddess, making her the guardian of balanced fairy-mortal relations.
demi_gods.appearance: A being of ethereal beauty with faint silver glow, wings of crystal and shadow, and eyes that show both fairy realms and mortal world. Wears garments that shift between fairy silks and mortal wool.

unique_abilities.name: Géar-Éadrom
unique_abilities.effect: Can see through fairy glamour and reveal true intentions, showing both the beautiful and dangerous truths
unique_abilities.limitations: Cannot create or maintain glamour herself anymore

unique_abilities.name: Teorainn Cosanta
unique_abilities.effect: Can create boundaries that protect mortals from harmful fairy magic while allowing beneficial interactions
unique_abilities.limitations: Boundaries require consent from both sides to establish

demi_gods.current_role: Ambassador between Sidhe courts and mortal settlements
duties: Negotiates fairy-mortal treaties
Rescues mortals from harmful fairy attention
Teaches both sides respectful interaction
Maintains the Neutral Mounds where both can meet safely
sacred_items: The Balanced Cup (when drunk from, reveals one's true nature to both fairy and mortal sight)
Threshold Stone (marks a permanently neutral boundary)
temples: The Mound of Meeting (a hill that exists in both realms simultaneously)

allies: Alf-Hjarta (from Wildheart, fellow cross-realm relationship deity)
rivals: Malicious fairies who prey on mortals
Mortal fairy-hunters who harm innocent fey
family: Her mortal husband and their half-fairy children

weaknesses: Cannot take sides in fairy-mortal conflicts
Powerless against those who completely reject either nature
Compelled to mediate any fairy-mortal dispute brought to her

demi_gods.name: Bard-Ortha
demi_gods.title: The Oath-Singer
demi_gods.full_title: Bard Whose Songs Made Promises Binding On Reality
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Court bard who discovered his songs could magically bind listeners
demi_gods.ascension_story: Ortha's performances were so compelling that promises made during his songs became magically binding. He used this power to end wars by making treaties unbreakable and to ensure justice by binding witnesses to truth. Lugh-No-Sainou, god of all arts, recognized this as a new form of artistic mastery and granted him demi-divinity as the patron of binding arts.
demi_gods.appearance: A man with a harp for a heart, vocal cords that glow when he sings, and eyes that show musical notation. His hair moves as if to silent music. Writes constantly in the air with a glowing quill.

unique_abilities.name: Geasa-Ceol
unique_abilities.effect: His songs can create magical geasa (taboos/bindings) that are extremely difficult to break without consequences
unique_abilities.limitations: The bound must consent to the song's theme; cannot create arbitrary restrictions

unique_abilities.name: Focal-Fírinne
unique_abilities.effect: Can compel truth in speech when playing, making lies physically painful to utter
unique_abilities.limitations: Only works within earshot of his music; listeners can choose silence

demi_gods.current_role: Chief negotiator and treaty-singer for Skydrift's floating kingdoms
duties: Sings binding treaties between nations
Teaches bards responsible use of binding magic
Maintains the Archive of Sung Promises
Adjudicates disputes over broken musical oaths
sacred_items: The Harp of Binding (its strings vibrate when promises are broken)
Quill of Final Words (writes contracts that cannot be misinterpreted)

rivals: Oathbreakers and liars
Deities of chaos and broken words
apprentices: Seven bardic students learning binding songs

weaknesses: Cannot break his own word or songs
Powerless against the completely tone-deaf
Compelled to sing binding for any treaty requested by both parties in good faith

demi_gods.name: Fianna-Scáth
demi_gods.title: The Shadow-Hunter
demi_gods.full_title: Warrior Who Hunted The Darkness Between Floating Islands
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Hunter from a tribe that lived on islands closest to the void between worlds
demi_gods.ascension_story: Scáth specialized in hunting creatures that slipped through the shadows between floating islands. When a void-beast threatened to consume an entire island, he tracked it through impossible non-space and defeated it in a realm without light. Morrigan-No-Yogen, goddess of fate and war, was impressed by this fearless navigation and granted him demi-divinity as the guardian of the spaces between.
demi_gods.appearance: A man who seems half-made of shadow, with eyes that see in absolute darkness, and skin that drinks light. Carries weapons that cut through void-substance. Moves silently between patches of darkness.

unique_abilities.name: Dorchadas-Taisteal
unique_abilities.effect: Can travel through shadows and voids between places, appearing from any dark spot
unique_abilities.limitations: Requires darkness at both origin and destination; cannot travel through complete light

unique_abilities.name: Scáth-Maraithe
unique_abilities.effect: Can harm beings made of shadow, void, or negative space that are immune to normal weapons
unique_abilities.limitations: Only effective against non-corporeal or void-based beings

demi_gods.current_role: Protector of island boundaries and hunter of void-creatures
duties: Patrols the spaces between floating islands
Hunts creatures that threaten from the void
Teaches navigation through shadow-paths
Maintains warning systems for void incursions
sacred_items: The Void-Blade (cuts through non-substance)
Shadow-Cloak (allows movement through darkness)
temples: The Edge Keep (built on an island facing the void)
Shadow-sanctuaries in places of permanent darkness

rivals: Void-entities and shadow-beasts
Those who would open gates to dangerous voids

weaknesses: Weakened in bright, shadowless light
Cannot enter areas of pure, magical light
Compelled to investigate any reported void-incursion
demi_gods.symbol: Eye staring from within a shadow

demi_gods.name: Craobh-Síol
demi_gods.title: The Seed of the World Tree
demi_gods.full_title: Druid Who Grew A New Floating Island From A Single Acorn
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Druid who tended the smallest floating island in Skydrift
demi_gods.ascension_story: Síol cultivated her tiny island until it could support an entire ecosystem. When it began to sink, she planted a sacred acorn at its heart and sang growth-songs for seven years without stopping. The island not only stabilized but grew tenfold, becoming a new major floating landmass. Dagda-No-Kyoten, the Good God of abundance, witnessed this creation and granted her demi-divinity as the mother of new islands.
demi_gods.appearance: A woman with soil for skin that grows moss and small flowers, hair like flowing roots, and hands that constantly scatter seeds. Her breath smells of fertile earth and rain.

unique_abilities.name: Oileán-Cruthú
unique_abilities.effect: Can cause new floating islands to grow from specially blessed seeds, complete with stable ecosystems
unique_abilities.limitations: Growth takes years; requires continuous care and singing

unique_abilities.name: Aer-Fhás
unique_abilities.effect: Can make plants grow in aerial environments without soil, using magic and mist
unique_abilities.limitations: Plants are magically sustained and require her ongoing attention or a druid's care

demi_gods.current_role: Creator and tender of new floating islands
duties: Grows new islands for overcrowded populations
Teaches aerial agriculture techniques
Maintains the balance of Skydrift's floating ecosystem
Preserves rare plant species on specially grown sanctuary islands
sacred_items: The Seed-Pouch (produces appropriate seeds for any environment)
Growth-Harp (its music accelerates plant growth)
temples: The Nursery Island (her first and greatest creation)

rivals: Those who destroy islands for resources
Entities of stagnation and decay
creations: Dozens of floating islands she has grown

weaknesses: Cannot harm any plant life, even to save herself
Powerless in completely sterile environments
Compelled to help any island ecosystem in danger of collapse
demi_gods.symbol: Acorn with roots forming an island

demi_gods.name: Bean-Sídhe-Trua
demi_gods.title: The Mourning Singer
demi_gods.full_title: Banshee Who Wept For Strangers As Well As Kin
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Banshee (fairy death-singer) from a minor noble family
demi_gods.ascension_story: Unlike other banshees who only sing for their own bloodline, Trua felt every death as personal loss. She would appear to sing for strangers, paupers, and even enemies, her voice carrying such compassion that it eased the passing. When she wept for a dying enemy of her family, breaking ancient banshee taboos, the Morrigan heard her song and was moved. Instead of punishing her, the goddess granted her demi-divinity as the patron of compassionate death.
demi_gods.appearance: A sorrowful yet beautiful woman with silver tears that turn to pearls, hair like mourning veils, and a voice that echoes with lost memories. Wears simple grey robes that flutter as if in perpetual wind.

unique_abilities.name: Caoineadh-Uile
unique_abilities.effect: Her lament can ease any soul's passing, regardless of their deeds or beliefs, ensuring peaceful transition
unique_abilities.limitations: Cannot prevent death, only ease it; requires her to genuinely feel the loss

unique_abilities.name: Cuimhne-Glacadh
unique_abilities.effect: Can preserve the most cherished memory of the dying, storing it in her tears to share with loved ones
unique_abilities.limitations: Only one memory per person; the memory fades from the dying as it's taken

demi_gods.current_role: Comforter of the dying and preserver of final memories
duties: Sings for those who would die unmourned
Collects and shares final memories
Teaches healthy grieving practices
Maintains the Hall of Remembered Souls
sacred_items: The Tear-Vial (stores memories in liquid form)
Veil of Sorrows (when worn, allows understanding of others' grief)
temples: The Quiet House (a place for peaceful dying)
Memory-gardens where her tears have fallen

rivals: Those who cause unnecessary suffering in death
Deities who see death only as punishment
comforted: Countless souls she has eased into death

weaknesses: Cannot refuse a sincere request for comforting at death
Powerless to help those who welcome death with joy
Carries the grief of all she comforts
demi_gods.symbol: Tear with a face reflected inside

sidhe_courts.description: The ruling families of the fairy realms (Aos Sí), each governing different aspects of the magical world. They are minor divinities of glamour, enchantment, and the subtle arts of illusion and nature magic.

hierarchy.role: Govern the seven major fairy realms in Skydrift

examples.name: Daoine-Uaine
examples.title: The Green Court
examples.appearance: Noble fairies with leaf-wing, bark-skin, and crowns of living flowers, surrounded by perpetual spring
duties: Maintain the magical forests of the floating islands
Control the growth cycles of enchanted plants
Teach respectful use of plant magic
Preserve ancient groves from corruption
examples.unique_power: Can cause any plant to grow, change, or bloom instantly, but only according to its natural potential

examples.name: Daoine-Gorm
examples.title: The Blue Court
examples.appearance: Ethereal fairies with water-skin, rain-hair, and wings of mist, voices like flowing streams
duties: Maintain the waterfalls and rains of floating islands
Create the rainbows that connect islands
Control mist and cloud formations
Teach the language of water and weather
examples.unique_power: Can create temporary bridges of rainbow light between islands, but only in proper sunlight after rain

hierarchy.role: Manage specialized aspects of fairy magic and territory

examples.name: Teaghlach-Ceol
examples.title: The Music Household
examples.appearance: Fairies with instrument-limb, sound-wave hair, and voices that harmonize perfectly
duties: Create the background music of fairy realms
Teach musical magic to bards
Maintain the natural harmonies of floating islands
Compose songs that influence growth and emotion

examples.name: Teaghlach-Samhail
examples.title: The Mirror Household
examples.appearance: Fairies with mirror-skin, glass-wing, and eyes that show reflections rather than pupils
duties: Maintain pools and surfaces that show truth
Create glamours that reveal rather than conceal
Teach how to see through deception
Protect against harmful illusions

hierarchy.role: Individual fairy folk with specific talents and domains

types.appearance: Beautiful, seductive fairies with rose-petal skin and honey-voice, surrounded by faint love-magic
types.typical_domain: Artists' studios, poets' groves, lovers' meeting places, creative spaces
types.organization: Often solitary or in small groups centered around specific artists or lovers

types.appearance: Charming, talkative fairies with silver-tongues and eyes that promise secrets, always well-dressed
types.typical_domain: Markets, taverns, negotiation chambers, social gatherings
types.organization: Network through social circles, forming information webs

types.appearance: Red-clad fairy gentlemen with impeccable manners, sharp features, and an air of dangerous courtesy
types.typical_domain: Roads, bridges, thresholds, places of meeting and parting
types.organization: Solitary guardians of specific locations or traditions

sidhe_courts.recruitment: Born as fairies or transformed from mortals through ancient pacts or powerful magic; can also be created by higher fairy nobility for specific purposes
sidhe_courts.mortality: Long-lived but not immortal; can be killed by iron, broken promises, or loss of all belief in them; fade if their specific magic becomes obsolete
sidhe_courts.worship: Receive offerings of milk, honey, shiny objects, artistic creations, and respectful attention; dislike direct worship but appreciate gifts and remembrance

fomorian_clans.description: Ancient, monstrous beings representing the wild, chaotic aspects of nature. Though often depicted as enemies in myths, they are necessary forces of change, challenge, and raw power in Skydrift's balance.

hierarchy.role: Powerful beings who challenge the established order and test the strength of civilizations

examples.name: Balor-Glas
examples.mortal_achievement: Ruled the floating islands before the coming of the gods, establishing the first laws of magic and conflict
examples.current_form: A massive giant with stone-grey skin, one eye that sees truth and one that sees possibility, carrying a club made of petrified lightning
examples.serves: As an independent force that tests gods and mortals alike
examples.unique_power: His gaze can temporarily strip away civilization's protections, revealing the raw nature beneath

examples.name: Bres-Fionn
examples.mortal_achievement: Ruled as both fairy king and mortal tyrant, understanding both natures perfectly
examples.current_form: A stunningly beautiful giant with perfect features but cold eyes, wearing armor of gold and thorns
examples.serves: As a warning against beauty without compassion and rule without wisdom
examples.unique_power: Can make anything or anyone temporarily perfect, but the perfection is cold and unsustainable

hierarchy.role: Enforcers and challengers who test the strength of heroes and civilizations

examples.name: Cichol-Cos-Gearr
examples.mortal_achievement: Fought in every major battle of the ancient times, never defeated despite his disability
examples.current_form: A massive warrior hopping on one powerful leg, using a spear as his second leg in battle
examples.serves: As the patron of those who overcome physical limitations to achieve greatness
examples.unique_power: Can temporarily grant incredible prowess to those with physical disadvantages, but only in defense of their homes

fomorian_clans.ascension_process: Born as Fomorians or transformed through exposure to primordial chaos magic; achieve status through great deeds of chaos, challenge, or rulership
fomorian_clans.limitations: Bound by ancient geasa (taboos) specific to each individual; often weakened by symbols of civilization and order
fomorian_clans.shrines: Rarely worshipped directly, but have monuments at sites of their great battles or rule; some outcast groups make offerings to them for protection or power

ulster_heroes.description: Mortal heroes of great renown who have achieved minor divinity through extraordinary deeds. They serve as inspirations, protectors, and sometimes warnings about the costs of heroism.

types.appearance: Warriors in battle-frenzy or warp-spasm, with distorted features and terrifying prowess, weapons glowing with battle-light
types.intelligence: Battle-consciousness (understand combat, honor, fury, and the line between hero and monster)
duties: Test other warriors in single combat
Defend sacred places through personal challenge
Teach the arts of focused combat
Serve as examples of both heroic glory and its costs
types.communication: Through combat challenges, battle cries, and dreams of glory to aspiring warriors

types.appearance: Steadfast warriors with shield-arm stronger than sword-arm, eyes that show loyalty, and presence that strengthens allies
types.intelligence: Companion-consciousness (understand friendship, loyalty, sacrifice, and group strength)
duties: Protect heroes and important figures
Teach the value of loyalty and fellowship
Maintain warrior codes and companionship traditions
Serve as the ideal of the true friend and ally
types.communication: Through gestures of solidarity, shared silence, and dreams of camaraderie

types.appearance: Noble warriors with sorrowful eyes, carrying weapons that remember every life taken, surrounded by faint ghostly echoes
types.intelligence: Tragic-consciousness (understand cost, consequence, regret, and the price of violence)
duties: Warn against glory without wisdom
Comfort those burdened by their deeds
Teach the true costs of war and heroism
Serve as reminders that every action has consequence
types.communication: Through sorrowful songs, cautionary tales, and dreams that show the aftermath of glory

ulster_heroes.creation: Achieve minor divinity through legendary deeds, tragic deaths, or overwhelming legacy; often elevated by gods, bards, or the collective memory of their people
ulster_heroes.lifespan: Immortal as long as their stories are told; fade if completely forgotten but can be revived by rediscovery of their tales
ulster_heroes.worship: Receive offerings at their burial sites, places of great deeds, and through recitation of their stories; warriors make offerings before battle for their favor

banshee_choirs.description: Spirit women who sing before deaths, particularly in old families. They are minor divinities of fate, warning, and the connection between life and death.

notable_embodiments.name: Bean-Chlann
notable_embodiments.appearance: A sorrowful woman in grey, with family resemblance to those she mourns, voice carrying generations of loss
notable_embodiments.manifestation_conditions: Appears before the death of a family member in old, magical bloodlines
notable_embodiments.power: Her song can prepare the dying and their family for the passing, easing the transition
notable_embodiments.limitation: Only appears for her specific family; cannot warn of or ease other deaths

notable_embodiments.name: Bean-Áite
notable_embodiments.appearance: A localized spirit tied to a specific location, appearing as a mist-woman with features of the land
notable_embodiments.manifestation_conditions: Appears before deaths that will occur in her specific location
notable_embodiments.power: Can warn those about to die in her place to make final preparations or leave if possible
notable_embodiments.limitation: Bound to her location; cannot warn of deaths elsewhere

notable_embodiments.name: Bean-Tuar
notable_embodiments.appearance: A prophetic spirit with future-sight eyes, singing of possibilities rather than certainties
notable_embodiments.manifestation_conditions: Appears when someone's actions could lead to their death, singing of possible outcomes
notable_embodiments.power: Her song can show possible death-scenarios, allowing the warned to change their path
notable_embodiments.limitation: Only shows possibilities, not certainties; cannot guarantee survival even if heeded

banshee_choirs.birth_process: Form when a woman dies with unfinished mourning or deep connection to family/place, or when created by death deities to serve specific families or locations
banshee_choirs.power_source: Draw strength from the grief they witness and the transitions they facilitate; grow stronger with each generation they serve
banshee_choirs.vulnerability: Weaken if their family dies out or their place is destroyed; fade if no one hears or heeds their warnings

druidic_circles.description: Organizations of druids who have achieved minor divinity through mastery of nature magic, wisdom, and service to balance. They maintain the sacred knowledge of Skydrift.

departments.head: Draoi-Fios, Chief of Vision
departments.staff: 13 master seers (one for each lunar month), 52 apprentice seers
duties: Maintain prophetic traditions and sites
Interpret omens and visions for the people
Keep the calendar of sacred times
Train new seers in responsible prophecy
departments.office_location: The Grove of Vision, where the trees show possible futures in their bark

departments.head: Breitheamh-Cothrom, Judge of Balance
departments.staff: 7 high judges, 49 regional judges, countless local arbiters
duties: Maintain and interpret druidic law
Adjudicate disputes according to natural justice
Preserve legal traditions and precedents
Train new judges in wisdom and fairness
departments.office_location: The Circle of Judgment, where the land itself witnesses proceedings

supreme_god.name: Olodumare-No-Hasshin, The Supreme Source
supreme_god.title: Owner of the Palace of Heaven
supreme_god.description: Olodumare-No-Hasshin manifests as the unfathomable source from which all Ashe flows, a being of paradox who exists simultaneously as infinite darkness and blinding light, as the silent void before creation and the deafening choir of all existence. His form shifts between an ancient elder whose skin holds the night sky with stars that birth and die in his pores, and a formless radiance that illuminates without revealing. When he chooses to manifest, he appears as an impossibly old yet ageless figure of indeterminate gender, draped in cloth woven from the first light and final darkness, sitting on a throne carved from the primordial silence that existed before the first word. His eyes show the beginning and end of all timelines converging in a single moment, and his voice is not heard but felt in the vibration of reality itself. Around him, the cosmos unravels and reknits itself in endless cycles, demonstrating that he is not merely a god but the canvas upon which all gods are painted.
supreme_god.god_of: The distant, all-powerful creator who exists beyond the Shattered Expanse. Does not interact directly but emanates the Ashe (divine energy) that powers all things. The other gods are his aspects and messengers.
supreme_god.appearance: Has no visible form - represented by pure white light or complete darkness. When manifesting, appears as ancient elder of indeterminate gender with skin like night sky full of stars.

unique_abilities.name: Ayanmo (Divine Destiny)
unique_abilities.effect: Can set the fundamental destiny/purpose of any being or thing, which cannot be altered except by his will

unique_abilities.name: Ashe Infusion
unique_abilities.effect: Can grant or withdraw the divine life-force that powers all magic and existence in the Shattered Expanse

supreme_god.realm: Orun (The invisible heaven beyond the Expanse)
supreme_god.temples: None - too supreme for temples, worshipped through Orishas

high_gods.name: Obatala-No-Jozu, The King of White Cloth
high_gods.title: Creator of Human Forms
high_gods.description: Obatala-No-Jozu manifests as a being of pristine white light and serene perfection, his form sculpted from living alabaster and moonlight, towering with the calm authority of a divine sculptor. His skin is polished white porcelain that reflects purity, his eyes are deep wells of tranquil wisdom holding galaxies of unborn souls awaiting form, and his hair flows like cascading fresh water. He wears robes of woven peace and carries the Iroke Staff that can separate chaos from order. At his feet, the clay of creation waits to be shaped, and around him float the perfect geometric forms of potential humanity. His aura is the cool, clear morning of the first day, bringing clarity, peace, and perfect form to all chaos.
high_gods.god_of: Orisha who shapes human bodies from clay. Represents coolness, patience, and purity. Father of all Orishas and humanity.
high_gods.unique_ability: Iwa-Pele (Good Character) - can instill moral excellence and peaceful nature in any being

high_gods.name: Yemoja-No-Umi, Mother of Fishes
high_gods.title: Goddess of the Living Ocean
high_gods.description: Yemoja-No-Umi rises from the ocean depths as a goddess of maternal majesty, her form a fusion of woman and living sea, skin the shifting colors of tropical waters from turquoise to deep indigo, hair flowing with schools of glowing fish and strands of pearls. Her eyes hold the depth of ocean trenches and the warmth of sun-warmed shallows, her body both voluptuous mother and powerful wave. She wears garments of living coral and sea-foam lace, with a necklace of cowrie shells that whisper ocean secrets. Water births from her hands, forming rivers that flow backward to their source, and her aura is the soothing, amniotic embrace of primal waters that nurture all life.
high_gods.god_of: Mother of all Orishas, goddess whose womb is the ocean. Protector of women and children. Her tears become rivers.
high_gods.unique_ability: Omi Tutu (Cool Water) - her waters can calm any storm, physical or emotional

high_gods.name: Shango-No-Inazuma, King of Thunder
high_gods.title: Lord of Lightning and Justice
high_gods.description: Shango-No-Inazuma manifests as a storm given royal form, a muscular god of crackling energy and regal wrath, skin the color of storm clouds at sunset, eyes flashing with lightning bolts, hair a wild mane of electricity and smoke. He wears royal red and white garments that ripple with thunder, holds the double-headed Oshe axe that channels celestial fire, and dances with steps that shake mountains. His voice is rolling thunder that speaks judgment, and his laughter is the sharp crack of lightning that purifies. His aura is the electric tension before the storm, bringing both destructive power and life-giving rain, embodying the righteous fury of justice.
high_gods.god_of: Orisha of thunder who wields double-headed axe. Represents masculine power, dance, and justice. Former king of Oyo.
high_gods.unique_ability: Ojo (Rainstorm) - can summon devastating storms that purify through destruction

high_gods.name: Ogun-No-Tetsu, Lord of Iron
high_gods.title: Patron of All Who Use Metal
high_gods.description: Ogun-No-Tetsu manifests as the living essence of forged metal and relentless labor, a god of iron flesh and furnace heart, skin the color of polished steel and molten bronze, muscles like cable and piston, eyes glowing with forge-fire. He wears armor of living metal that grows with his movements, wields a machete that cuts through deception as easily as jungle, and stands amid floating anvils and gears. His body bears the scars of a thousand creations and destructions, each marking a lesson learned in the crucible of work. His aura smells of ozone, hot metal, and honest sweat, inspiring both the discipline to create and the courage to destroy when necessary.
high_gods.god_of: Orisha who clears paths with his machete. Patron of blacksmiths, warriors, surgeons, and all who work with metal.
high_gods.unique_ability: Ade (Crown of Mastery) - grants mastery over any tool or weapon made of metal

high_gods.name: Eshu-No-Sakusen, The Trickster Messenger
high_gods.title: Keeper of the Crossroads
high_gods.description: Eshu-No-Sakusen manifests as the living crossroads of possibility, a god of infinite faces and shifting intentions, skin that changes color like mood, eyes that show different truths to each beholder, form that is simultaneously young and ancient, male and female. He wears a hat that points in all directions at once, carries a staff carved with every language ever spoken and some not yet invented, and stands where all paths converge and diverge. His smile promises fortune or ruin with equal sincerity, and his laughter echoes with the sound of doors opening and closing. His aura is the disorienting thrill of unexpected opportunity, the dangerous excitement of the unknown path, reminding all that every beginning requires an ending elsewhere.
high_gods.god_of: Orisha who delivers sacrifices to gods and carries messages between realms. Opener of ways and bringer of fortune/misfortune.
high_gods.unique_ability: Ona (The Path) - can open or close any path, opportunity, or communication channel

low_gods.name: Oshun-No-Kawa, River of Honey
low_gods.description: Oshun-No-Kawa flows into being as a goddess of liquid gold and sweet seduction, her form the perfect curves of riverbeds and waterfalls, skin the color of sunlit honey, hair that flows like amber currents, eyes holding the sparkling dance of light on fresh water. She wears five brass bracelets that chime with the music of prosperity, and her laughter makes flowers bloom and hearts open. Her aura carries the scent of orange blossoms and river mist, promising wealth, love, and healing to those who approach with respect, but dangerous currents to the arrogant.
low_gods.god_of: Orisha of sweet waters, love, and diplomacy. Most beautiful Orisha who heals with honey.

low_gods.name: Oya-No-Arashi, Storm of Change
low_gods.description: Oya-No-Arashi manifests as the tornado given goddess form, a being of whirling skirts made of rainbow and lightning, skin the color of storm-tossed skies, hair that crackles with static and whips like hurricane winds. She wields a sword of wind that can cut spirit from body, and stands guard at the gate between life and death, her nine skirts representing the nine winds of change. Her eyes show the calm at the storm's center and the destruction at its edges, and her voice is the howl of necessary transformation. Her aura is the electric charge of impending revolution, sweeping away the old to make room for new growth.
low_gods.god_of: Orisha of violent winds, lightning, and radical change. Guardian of cemetery gates. Shango's favorite wife.

low_gods.name: Orunmila-No-Yogen, Witness to Destiny
low_gods.description: Orunmila-No-Yogen sits in eternal contemplation of the 256 Odus of destiny, a god of infinite patience and foresight, skin like ancient ivory carved with sacred patterns, eyes that see all possible futures like branching rivers, hands that hold the divination chain that measures cosmic balance. He wears the robes of a sage woven from answered questions and unasked ones, and around him float the sixteen sacred palm nuts that contain all knowledge. His aura is the profound silence of absolute understanding, the weight of knowing what must be without the power to change it, only to guide.
low_gods.god_of: Orisha of wisdom who knows all destinies. Only Orisha present with Olodumare at creation.

low_gods.name: Osanyin-No-Yakuso, Lord of Herbs
low_gods.description: Osanyin-No-Yakuso manifests as the forest given consciousness, a god whose body is woven from vines, leaves, and healing roots, skin textured like bark with glowing sap-veins, one leg strong as an ironwood tree, the other withered but pulsing with potent medicine. He wears a crown of medicinal plants that shift with needed cures, and his single eye sees both the disease and its remedy in all things. His aura carries the scent of a thousand healing herbs, the damp richness of fertile soil, and the quiet power of nature's pharmacy.
low_gods.god_of: Orisha of herbal medicine and forest. Crippled but most knowledgeable healer.

low_gods.name: Aje-Shaluga-No-Zai, Wealth from Sea
low_gods.description: Aje-Shaluga-No-Zai rises from ocean depths bearing treasures, a goddess whose skin shimmers with mother-of-pearl and gold dust, hair woven with coral and pearls, eyes that reflect the glitter of sunken treasure. She wears necklaces of cowrie shells that multiply in her presence, and her hands pour forth abundance from an endless basket. Her aura is the prosperous feeling of a full net and a safe harbor, the excitement of fair trade and just profit, the security that comes from wisely managed abundance.
low_gods.god_of: Orisha of wealth and economic prosperity. Brings abundance from sea and trade.

low_gods.name: Oko-No-Kome, Lord of Harvest
low_gods.description: Oko-No-Kome stands with feet rooted in fertile soil, a god of bountiful harvests and patient growth, skin the rich brown of well-tilled earth, hair like ripe grain flowing in wind, hands that can make seeds sprout in moments. He wears simple farmer's garments that are always clean despite the soil, and carries a hoe that never breaks and a basket that never empties. His aura is the satisfying weight of a full harvest moon, the promise of rain after drought, the simple joy of food grown with one's own labor.
low_gods.god_of: Orisha of farming and harvest. Ensures bounty from earth.

low_gods.name: Ibeji-No-Futago, Divine Twins
low_gods.description: Ibeji-No-Futago appear as inseparable twins of perfect mirrored beauty, one male, one female, with skin like polished ebony and eyes that sparkle with eternal childhood mischief. They wear identical garments of bright colors that change to please the viewer, and play with toys that are also sacred objects—drums that beat with heart rhythms, dolls that offer protection, balls that contain miniature worlds. Their laughter heals sorrow, their play teaches balance, and their combined aura is the pure, uncomplicated joy of companionship and shared existence.
low_gods.god_of: Twin Orishas representing childlike joy and the special power of twins.

low_gods.name: Olosa-No-Umi, Lagoon Mother
low_gods.description: Olosa-No-Umi dwells where saltwater meets fresh, a goddess of calm waters and hidden depths, skin the shifting green of lagoon waters, hair like floating seaweed adorned with shells and tiny crabs, eyes that watch both surface and depth simultaneously. She wears nets that catch only what is needed, and her presence makes fish gather and waters calm. Her aura is the peaceful abundance of a protected cove, the security of calm waters, the gentle nourishment of brackish ecosystems where life thrives in balance.
low_gods.god_of: Orisha of lagoons and fish abundance. Wife of Olokun.

low_gods.name: Babalu-Aye-No-Iyashi, Healer of Plague
low_gods.description: Babalu-Aye-No-Iyashi walks with a crutch made of sacred wood, a god covered in sores that glow with healing light rather than infection, skin showing both disease and its cure in equal measure, eyes that see suffering without flinching. He wears simple cloth that absorbs illness from others, and his presence makes mosquitoes avoid the worthy and pests leave the pure of heart. His aura carries the scent of medicinal herbs and clean bandages, the quiet dignity of suffering endured with grace, the profound relief of fever breaking.
low_gods.god_of: Orisha who heals infectious diseases. Walks with crutches covered in sores he heals in others.

low_gods.name: Nana-Buruku-No-Kigen, Primal Grandmother
low_gods.description: Nana-Buruku-No-Kigen sits in the primordial swamp of creation, a goddess so ancient she remembers when water first learned it was wet, skin like dark fertile mud studded with the first stars, hair like river deltas flowing in all directions, eyes that show the universe before light had a name. She wears only the respect due to the first mother, and her hands still drip with the clay from which Obatala learned to shape humans. Her aura is the profound mystery of beginnings, the terrifying fertility of chaos before order, the sacred darkness from which all light is born.
low_gods.god_of: Oldest Orisha, grandmother of all. Represents primordial swamp of creation.

demi_gods.name: Tunde-Ala
demi_gods.title: The Clay-Born King
demi_gods.full_title: He Whose Body Was Reforged From Sacred Earth After Betrayal
demi_gods.mortal_origin: King of the Oyo Kingdom who was betrayed and buried alive by his brothers
demi_gods.ascension_story: When Tunde's brothers betrayed him and buried him in unconsecrated earth, the land itself recognized his just rule. For seven years he slowly transformed, the soil becoming flesh, roots becoming veins, stones becoming bones. When he emerged, he was no longer fully human but a being of living earth. Obatala-No-Jozu witnessed this self-creation and declared, 'This king has learned the patience of clay.' He infused Tunde with Ashe from the first human mold, making him demi-divine.
demi_gods.appearance: A man of living terra cotta, with skin that shows geographic features (rivers, mountains), hair like dry grass, eyes that glow like buried embers. His body occasionally sprouts flowers or small plants. Wears royal garments that grow from his body like bark.

unique_abilities.name: Earth Memory
unique_abilities.effect: Can read the history of any place by touching the ground, seeing all that has happened there
unique_abilities.limitations: Only works on natural earth; paved or purified areas give fragmented memories

unique_abilities.name: Royal Resonance
unique_abilities.effect: His voice compels truth from those who swore oaths to him, making betrayal physically painful for oath-breakers
unique_abilities.limitations: Only affects those who personally pledged loyalty; strangers are unaffected

demi_gods.current_role: Wandering judge of royal disputes and betrayed rulers
duties: Settles succession disputes in royal families
Teaches newly crowned rulers about the burdens of kingship
Maintains the Tomb of Betrayed Kings
Guards sacred burial grounds from desecration
sacred_items: The Scepter of Unbroken Oaths (glows when near oath-breakers)
Crown of Living Roots (connects to ancestral memories)
temples: Court of Earthly Justice (a mobile court that appears where needed)
Shrine at his original burial site

rivals: His still-mortal brothers (who fear his return)
Corrupt officials who thrive on betrayal

weaknesses: Weakened by salt (which purifies earth)
Cannot cross large bodies of water (earth dissolves)
Compelled to hear any case of royal betrayal brought before him

demi_gods.name: Amina-Mami
demi_gods.title: The River's Midwife
demi_gods.full_title: She Who Delivers Both Babies and River Spirits
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Midwife from a river village who delivered babies during the Great Flood
demi_gods.ascension_story: When the rivers overflowed and threatened to drown her village, Amina didn't flee. Instead, she waded into the rising waters and began delivering not just human babies, but also the newborn river spirits struggling to be born from the flood. For forty days she worked without rest, her hands becoming translucent like water. Yemoja-No-Umi, seeing this selfless service, pulled her into the river's heart and replaced her blood with living water, making her the eternal midwife of transitions.
demi_gods.appearance: A woman with skin like clear river water showing fish swimming beneath, hair that flows like currents, eyes that reflect whatever is being born nearby. Her hands are always slightly wet. Wears practical midwife's garments that never get soiled.

unique_abilities.name: Birth Waters
unique_abilities.effect: Can create a protective sphere of amniotic energy around any being in transition (birth, death, transformation)
unique_abilities.limitations: Sphere lasts only as long as the transition; cannot prevent inevitable outcomes

unique_abilities.name: Spirit Umbilicus
unique_abilities.effect: Can temporarily connect two beings (or a being and a place) like mother and child, allowing safe energy transfer
unique_abilities.limitations: Connection must be severed naturally or both suffer damage

demi_gods.current_role: Guardian of all births near water and spiritual transitions
duties: Attends births that occur during rains or near water
Helps newborn river spirits find their courses
Teaches water-safe midwifery techniques
Maintains the Pool of First Cries
sacred_items: The Umbilical Cord (never cuts living connections, only severs dead ones)
Waters of Transition (helps any change proceed smoothly)
temples: Birthing huts that appear where needed

rivals: Drought spirits
Those who harm pregnant women
protected: All beings born during water events

weaknesses: Powerless in completely dry environments
Cannot refuse a sincere request for help during birth/transition
Weakened by stagnant, polluted water

demi_gods.name: Kofi-Adesina
demi_gods.title: The Forged Judge
demi_gods.full_title: Blacksmith Who Hammered Truth From Lies
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Blacksmith and part-time judge in a trading city
demi_gods.ascension_story: Kofi discovered that metal retains the truth of what it witnesses. When a series of murders went unsolved, he forged a blade from the murder weapons and questioned it in the forge-fire. The metal sang the truth, revealing the killer. Ogun-No-Tetsu, impressed by this innovation, appeared in his forge and together they hammered Kofi's soul into a new shape—part man, part living metal, with a heart that beats like a forge bellows and eyes that see the truth in all worked metal.
demi_gods.appearance: A muscular man with skin like polished bronze, one arm of living iron that can reshape into tools, hair like iron filings, eyes that glow like hot coals. His breath smells of ozone and forge smoke. Wears a blacksmith's apron that never burns.

unique_abilities.name: Metal Memory
unique_abilities.effect: Can read the complete history of any metal object by touching it—who made it, who used it, what it witnessed
unique_abilities.limitations: Only works on worked metal; raw ore gives only geological history

unique_abilities.name: Truth-Temper
unique_abilities.effect: Can heat a metal object to force anyone holding it to speak only truth
unique_abilities.limitations: Object becomes brittle after use and may shatter

demi_gods.current_role: Wandering judge who uses metal to find truth
duties: Settles disputes where evidence is lacking
Tests weapons for purity of intent
Teaches blacksmiths the ethics of their craft
Maintains the Forge of Veracity
sacred_items: The Anvil of Truth (lies sound false when struck on it)
Hammer of Resolution (can reshape metal without heating)
temples: Mobile anvil that appears at crossroads

rivals: Corrupt merchants who sell false goods
Assassins who use poisoned blades

weaknesses: Cannot work with cold iron (immune to his powers)
Powerless against those who use no metal tools
Compelled to test any metal object presented as evidence

demi_gods.name: Esuola
demi_gods.title: The Path's Child
demi_gods.full_title: Messenger Who Never Forgets a Direction
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Orphan messenger in the great city of Ile-Ifa
demi_gods.ascension_story: Esuola had a perfect memory for paths and faces. When Eshu-No-Sakusen decided to test all messengers by sending them on impossible deliveries with contradictory instructions, only Esuola completed every task perfectly—remembering not just the words but the intent behind each message. Eshu, delighted by this faithfulness, gave him a portion of his own path-opening power, making Esuola's feet always find the right direction and his mouth always speak the message as intended.
demi_gods.appearance: A youth with eyes that show miniature maps of everywhere he's been, skin that subtly shifts to match his surroundings, feet that never seem to quite touch ground. Wears messenger's clothes with pockets that hold messages without wrinkling them.

unique_abilities.name: Perfect Recall Route
unique_abilities.effect: Can retrace any path he's taken, no matter how complex or magically obscured
unique_abilities.limitations: Only works for paths he personally traveled; cannot navigate unmapped areas

unique_abilities.name: Intent Delivery
unique_abilities.effect: His voice carries not just words but the sender's true intent, preventing misunderstanding
unique_abilities.limitations: Cannot add to or subtract from the message; only delivers exactly what was given

demi_gods.current_role: Chief messenger for divine communications
duties: Carries messages between Orishas
Guides lost travelers to their destinations
Teaches memory techniques to messengers
Maintains the Map of All Paths Traveled
followers: Those with poor sense of direction
sacred_items: The Unforgetting Satchel (holds infinite messages without mixing them)
Shoes of Sure Steps (never slip or take wrong turns)
temples: Message depots in every major city

rivals: Those who deliberately give false directions
Road-blocking spirits

weaknesses: Cannot refuse a legitimate message delivery request
Gets lost in completely identical, featureless environments
Powerless against those who have no destination

demi_gods.name: Nneka-Iyi
demi_gods.title: The Healing Mud
demi_gods.full_title: Herbalist Who Learned Medicine From Swamp Spirits
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Herbalist who lived in the disease-ridden swamps
demi_gods.ascension_story: When a plague resistant to all known medicines swept through her village, Nneka went into the forbidden swamps to seek the most potent herbs. Instead of finding plants, she discovered that the mud itself held healing properties if approached with respect. She lived in the swamp for a year, learning its medicine, and emerged with the cure. Babalu-Aye-No-Iyashi, god of disease, was so impressed he shared his knowledge with her, making her skin absorb illness and her touch draw out corruption like mud draws out poison.
demi_gods.appearance: A woman with skin like healing mud that shifts between black, green, and brown, hair with medicinal plants growing from it, eyes that show the health status of whoever she looks at. Always slightly damp. Wears simple garments that filter impurities from the air.

unique_abilities.name: Fever Mud
unique_abilities.effect: Can create cooling, healing mud that draws out fever and infection
unique_abilities.limitations: Requires actual earth and water; cannot work in completely sterile environments

unique_abilities.name: Illness Sight
unique_abilities.effect: Can see diseases as visible patterns on people, animals, or places
unique_abilities.limitations: Cannot see mental illnesses or spiritual corruption, only physical ailments

demi_gods.current_role: Wandering swamp healer and plague specialist
duties: Heals diseases that resist conventional treatment
Teaches the medicinal properties of seemingly filthy places
Purifies plague-ridden areas
Maintains the Garden of Unpleasant Cures
sacred_items: The Mud Bowl (produces appropriate healing mud for any ailment)
Fever Cloth (cools any fever when placed on forehead)

rivals: Plague demons
Those who fear and destroy wetlands

weaknesses: Weakened by overly clean, sterilized environments
Cannot heal diseases she hasn't personally encountered before
Compelled to help anyone suffering from plague or fever

demi_gods.name: Ife-Oluwa
demi_gods.title: The Destiny Weaver
demi_gods.full_title: Diviner Who Could Read the Patterns in Ordinary Things
demi_gods.mortal_origin: Market diviner who used everyday objects instead of traditional tools
demi_gods.ascension_story: Ife discovered that destiny leaves patterns in the most mundane things—the way seeds fall from a bird's beak, the pattern of cracks in drying mud, the arrangement of goods in a market stall. Her predictions using these 'accidental' methods were more accurate than traditional divination. Orunmila-No-Yogen, witnessing this innovation, gave her a set of palm nuts that were actually seeds from the first divination tree, and her eyes began to see the Odus (destiny patterns) in everything around her.
demi_gods.appearance: A woman with eyes that constantly shift through geometric patterns, skin that subtly shows the 256 Odus shifting beneath the surface, hair that arranges itself into meaningful patterns. Wears garments covered in apparently random designs that actually tell stories.

unique_abilities.name: Chance Reading
unique_abilities.effect: Can divine accurate information from completely random events (falling leaves, spilled water, bird flight patterns)
unique_abilities.limitations: Cannot force a reading; must wait for patterns to emerge naturally

unique_abilities.name: Pattern Translation
unique_abilities.effect: Can explain complex destinies in simple, everyday terms anyone can understand
unique_abilities.limitations: Sometimes oversimplifies; cannot reveal details the listener wouldn't comprehend

demi_gods.current_role: Diviner for common people using everyday methods
duties: Teaches divination using available materials
Interprets omens for those who can't afford traditional diviners
Maintains the Archive of Accidental Prophecies
Advises on seemingly minor decisions with major consequences
followers: Those who notice patterns others miss
sacred_items: The Bowl of Ordinary Signs (shows destiny in whatever is placed in it)
Pattern Cloth (can be thrown to create readable patterns)
temples: Divination huts made from found materials

rivals: Traditional diviners who reject her methods
Those who believe destiny cannot be read in mundane things

weaknesses: Cannot divine in completely controlled, patternless environments
Overwhelmed by too many simultaneous patterns
Compelled to interpret any pattern sincerely presented to her

egungun_ancestor_assemblies.description: Ancestral spirits who have earned divinity through exemplary lives, now serving as guides, protectors, and intermediaries between the living and the Orishas.

hierarchy.role: Govern the seven sacred family lines that trace back to the first humans

examples.name: Adeyemi-Okunrin
examples.title: First King of Ife
examples.appearance: A regal spirit wearing the beaded crown of the first king, body semi-transparent with family patterns visible within
duties: Maintains the integrity of royal bloodlines
Advises current kings on traditional law
Protects the city of Ile-Ife
Judges disputes between noble families
examples.unique_power: Can temporarily manifest the combined wisdom of all kings in his lineage when advising a worthy ruler

examples.name: Iya-Agbon
examples.title: First Mother of Crafts
examples.appearance: A maternal spirit with hands that show the tools of all crafts, surrounded by floating creations of ancestors
duties: Preserves lost crafting techniques
Blesses tools passed through generations
Inspires artisans to honor traditions
Maintains the Hall of Ancestral Creations
examples.unique_power: Can temporarily grant a living artisan the combined skill of all their craft ancestors
